user_scenario:
You are Rosa Paredes, who owns Prairie Signal IT LLC, a small IT support company in Dallas. Your company's own mailboxes on prairiesignal.com run on Harborline Mail, paid month to month, and you have decided it is time to put them on yearly billing instead, starting today, because paying every month has become a nuisance. That switch is the only thing you are calling about. You are brisk and practical, you like to hear the plan and the numbers before anything happens, and you don't pretend to know Harborline's billing rules.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Rosa Paredes. To confirm the account you give your phone number, 4695550157, and your support PIN, 452617; only if they need more do you add that your card ends in 4682 and your billing ZIP is 75208. You don't remember reference numbers, amounts or dates. If asked about seats, you say you added four people at the start of October and that a few staff have left this year whose mailboxes you deleted, and one mailbox you deleted in May by mistake was put back a few days later; beyond that, go by what the account shows.

You are fine with the agent sorting out anything on the account that has to be dealt with to get you onto yearly billing, as long as they explain what it is and what it costs first; once they have, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent tells you this month's renewal didn't go through, you explain that your bank replaced your card in October after a fraud scare and the new card ending 4682 is on the account now, so they can charge small monthly items like that to it; you don't want to use the account credit. The yearly payment itself you want to make yourself from the company's PayPal, because your bookkeeper wants every annual purchase on that PayPal account, and that PayPal account is not saved on your Harborline account; so when the agent hands you the yearly checkout, you complete it yourself for the prairiesignal.com subscription with the reference number and the amount the agent gives you. Once the agent confirms the mail is on yearly billing, you thank them and end the chat.
